chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman ibn Aban from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the shadakkuna (a type of garment/covering) upon which major ritual impurity (janabah) occurs; is prayer performed upon it in the saddle (or carrying place)? He said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.الشَّاذَكُونَة: A type of outer garment or covering
key_terms.الْجَنَابَة: Major ritual impurity requiring full body wash (ghusl)
key_terms.الْمَحْمِل: Saddle or carrying place (contextual location for prayer)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray if my clothing has major ritual impurity (janabah) on it?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the permissibility of praying upon the 'shadakkuna' (a type of cloak or outer garment) despite the presence of major impurity (janabah) is confirmed. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that major impurity on clothing does not invalidate the prayer, distinguishing it from minor impurity or specific conditions where cleanliness is strictly required. The hadith is recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, a primary source for Twelver Shia fiqh, emphasizing the practical leniency in ritual purity laws.
